title: Construct a low-exposure bridge and control its complete weak-loss error
statement: Three exact stages give T=[pi/(2tan(phi))+2phi]/Omega, A_e=[pi*sin(phi)*cos(phi)/2+phi-sin(2phi)/2]/Omega and2A_a+A_e=T. The smallphi product approachespi^2/(4Omega^2). For0<=Gamma<=kappa I, complete Markov error squared differs from ideal dose by at most3(kappa*T)^2/4+(kappa*T)^3/12.

Markov conclusions need the declared positive loss operator/dilation. provides: Three exact stages give T=[pi/(2tan(phi))+2phi]/Omega, A_e=[pi*sin(phi)*cos(phi)/2+phi-sin(2phi)/2]/Omega and2A_a+A_e=T. The smallphi product approachespi^2/(4Omega^2). For0<=Gamma<=kappa I, complete Markov error squared differs from ideal dose by at most3(kappa*T)^2/4+(kappa*T)^3/12.
assumptions: An ideal Markov dose is not an exact floor for arbitrary closed radiation. Occupation alone gives no uniform finite-band radiation floor without temporal/control resources. A nontrivial collective kernel alone does not supply controllability; independent channels can remove it. Dipole formulas are free-space point-dipole Born–Markov/RWA estimates with paid exchange, not a universal device constraint.

body: Storage loss makes very long low-emitter paths costly: dose>=2sqrt(2kappa_p(kappa_e-kappa_p))/Omega. The simple asymptotic construction is within factorpi/(2sqrt2), not globally exact optimum. Orthogonal emitted sectors and actual no-jump updates are needed; normalized surviving-state error discards the loss contribution. Photon production, Jacobi capture/release and flags are excluded from the local-gate numeric example.
